title: CoreWeave, Nvidia Credit Risk Hit Fresh Highs
summary: Bloomberg's James Crombie joins Dani Burger on "Bloomberg Deals." CoreWeave and Nvidia credit-risk measures hit fresh all-time highs Wednesday while gauges of perceived worry again reached levels last seen in March, as Wall Street grew increasingly concerned about the tech sector’s record borrowing to finance AI. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: S&P Says It May Downgrade Nvidia’s Ratings on Governance Worries
summary: S&P Global Ratings is looking at cutting Nvidia Corp.’s credit by one notch, citing concerns over the company’s management and governance following the departure, and then the return, of Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang.

title: Netflix to Buy Radford Studio Center for $380 Million
summary: Bloomberg's John Gittelsohn discusses Netflix’s purchase of the historic Radford Studio Center in Los Angeles. The $380 million price is about 80% below the $1.85 billion Hackman Capital Partners paid for the property in 2021. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Can US Chip Controls Slow China’s AI Progress?
summary: Nvidia is at the center of a renewed debate over how much access China should have to advanced US AI chips. CSIS’s Emily Harding discusses whether export controls can meaningfully slow China’s AI progress without accelerating its domestic chip industry, what lawmakers should ask Jensen Huang when he testifies before Congress, and why technology companies increasingly need to think of themselves as potential national security targets. She joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: US Genesis Mission Looks to AI to Accelerate Science
summary: One year after the launch of the Genesis Mission, the US Department of Energy says the AI-driven initiative has grown to nearly 300 research projects spanning energy, biology, advanced manufacturing and national security. DOE Undersecretary for Science Dario Gil discusses using AI to simulate the power grid 1,000 times faster, efforts to accelerate nuclear and fusion development, and the goal of doubling the productivity and impact of US research and development within a decade. He joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Nasdaq 100 Tumbles in ‘Sell First’ Mode
summary: Bloomberg’s Ed Ludlow takes a look at markets as the Nasdaq 100 touches bear-market territory with traders dumping tech shares. Plus, Nvidia shares also tumble after the return of CEO Jensen Huang, with the stock remaining down 35% from its October 6 peak; and Under Secretary of Energy Dario Gil joins to discuss AI's role in national security on the one-year anniversary of President Trump's Genesis Mission. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: ElevenLabs in Early Talks for 2027 Funding at $33 Billion Value
summary: ElevenLabs, an artificial intelligence company focused on realistic-sounding voices, is in early discussions for a funding round at a target valuation of $33 billion, according to people familiar with the matter.

title: Fast Fixes for Cyber Flaws Mean Tech Outages Likely to Continue
summary: AI is a key factor.

title: SpaceX Receives Government Approval to Launch Space Data Centers
summary: The US Federal Communications Commission approved SpaceX’s request to launch as many as 1 million satellites for Elon Musk’s vision to build a network of data centers in orbit for complex artificial intelligence computing.

title: AI Debt Financing Story Is Far From Over: Cisar
summary: Winnie Cisar, global head of strategy at CreditSights, says AI infrastructure spending should remain robust into 2027 even as credit spreads widen and financing gets more expensive. Investors will increasingly scrutinize returns on planned projects, she says on “Bloomberg Surveillance.” (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Tech Stocks Tumble in ‘Sell First’ Mode as AI Angst Fuels Losses
summary: The Nasdaq 100 Index tumbled for a second day, sending it briefly careening into bear-market territory, as mounting fears about over-investment in AI pummeled shares of the biggest technology companies. Bloomberg's Michael Ball joins to discuss. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Nasdaq 100 Enters Bear Market
summary: Get a jump start on the US trading day with Dani Burger on "Bloomberg Open Interest." Another brutal day for the AI trade. The Nasdaq 100 enters bear-market territory as the global tech rout deepens. President Trump rebuilds his tariff wall, targeting China, Europe and other major trading partners. And Treasuries rally as fresh inflation data keeps a December Fed hike in play. White House economic adviser Kevin Hassett joins Bloomberg Open Interest on what he calls a “goldilocks” economy, rates and the road ahead. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Copper Can’t Escape the AI Trade Yet: Gower
summary: Amy Gower, lead metals and mining strategist at Morgan Stanley, says copper remains tied to the AI trade as tech volatility weighs on the metal. Morgan Stanley still expects a copper deficit next year and sees an overshoot as a buying opportunity, she says on “Bloomberg Surveillance.” (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Fed, AI Fears Rattle Markets
summary: Stocks slide as investors question whether the AI boom can deliver profits soon enough. Bloomberg’ Macro Strategist Michael Ball and Ira Jersey, Chief US Rates Strategist at Bloomberg Intelligence discuss the market’s selloff, Treasury demand, oil-price risks, and what the Fed’s next moves could mean for yields. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Power On: What to Make of Cook’s Relationship with Trump
summary: A 70-year-old Apple fan who still owns his original iPhone wrote in to ask: Why is Tim Cook making so many concessions to Donald Trump—and will John Ternus change things? On the Power On podcast, Mark Gurman breaks down the tension inside Apple over Tim Cook’s political playbook. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: J.P. Morgan’s Rosenbaum on 2027 AI Spend
summary: Nathaniel Rosenbaum, JPMorgan’s Head of U.S. High-Grade Credit Strategy, expects another busy year of AI-related borrowing but says issuance growth could crest during 2027. High-grade supply surged nearly three and a half times this year, he said; next year, it could reach a record $2.1 trillion without repeating that jump. He speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Nasdaq 100 Enters Bear Market Territory as AI Angst Fuels Losses
summary:
The Nasdaq 100 Index plunged for a second day, sending it careening into bear-market territory as traders dumped technology shares, with worries around AI dominating sentiment on Wall Street.
Bloomberg US Equities Team Lead, Elena Popina discusses AI sentiment and the ongoing rout in tech shares. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Deere Down on Earnings; Dell Lower Despite Server Sales | Stock Movers
summary:
On this episode of Stock Movers:

- Deere (DE) shares are lower as it reports earnings this morning, with the focus of investors being on the farm economy and whether it will emerge from a prolonged slump that's pressured sales of tractors and other agricultural equipment. Deere reported earnings per share for the fourth quarter that missed the average analyst estimate.
- Dell Technologies (DELL) is lower this morning even after it boosted its fiscal year revenue sales outlook for the third time due to surging server sales fueled by the rapid build-out of AI data centers.
- Nvidia (NVDA) and Anthropic (ANT) are lower as the broader AI trade continues to sink after the Jensen Huang-led rally. Anthropic has traded below their $83 initial public offering price for the first time, wiping out gains for investors who piled into the artificial intelligence lab’s record-setting debut last week. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Billions in Data Center Deals Grind to Halt After AI Chip Curbs
summary: Lenders have hit the brakes on billions of dollars in loans tied to Chinese firms ByteDance, Alibaba and Tencent, as new US curbs on chip access threaten to upend Asia’s burgeoning AI debt financing market.

title: HP Rises on Profit Outlook Signaling Tight Grip on Memory Costs
summary: HP Inc. shares jumped by as much as 15% after the company gave a profit forecast for the current year that will likely exceed analysts’ estimates, signaling the computer and printer maker is improving its ability to manage rising costs associated with memory chips.
